title: ArgSpec: entry points declare their own args; one parser rejects, helps, passes through

body:
## Summary
Give every dev entry point (and ArenaArgs, which every arena film goes through) one declarative arg contract. Each declares a const spec of flag -> {type, default, required, help} and hands it to core/args/ArgSpec. ArgSpec parses the args, rejects an unknown one with a did-you-mean and exit 2, prints generated usage on --help, and lets the game's own LaunchArgs.KNOWN_FLAGS pass through. This is not a registry: the spec lives in the script that reads the flag, and there is no central list, owner or expiry. It replaces 87 hand-written parse loops; it does not catalogue flags.

## Description
Today 87 files in project/dev read OS.get_cmdline_user_args raw (90 reads), each with its own loop. 66 of them quit(2) on some error and 20 never reject anything. 19 keep a local KNOWN list that has to repeat any game flag the script's callees read (rig_bench_run.gd:8; city_bench's list shares 4 flags with LaunchArgs). ArenaArgs (boot/arena_args.gd) accepts any string, and 13 dev files read 41 distinct flags through it. Meanwhile the debt ratchet blocks any new raw read (metrics.mjs:76), so a lane writing a new dev script has no sanctioned way to read its args. Lanes hit this as FRICTION in hud, handheld and perf on 2026-11-07. ArgSpec gives the ratchet somewhere to send them.

## Flow
- core/args/arg_spec.gd (RefCounted, engine-agnostic, about 150 LOC): new(spec); parse(args = OS.get_cmdline_user_args()) -> self; ok(), exit_code(), error(), usage(), and has/text/number/flag accessors. Pass-through is LaunchArgs.KNOWN_FLAGS when the autoload exists. Did-you-mean picks the declared flag with the smallest edit distance, if it is <= 2.
- ArenaArgs keeps its API (has/text/number) but builds on ArgSpec, with the 41 flags its readers use declared in one const. A bad arg takes arena_game.gd's existing quit path with exit 2.
- Migrate the 10 scripts in the write set (the benches and the frame/audio tools lanes run most). Each drops its loop and its raw read.
- Tighten the tools/debt baseline with --update, and add a DECISION line saying new dev entry points use ArgSpec.

## Expected impact
A misspelt or misplaced flag stops costing a film: it exits 2 in under a second and names the flag it meant. A new A/B flag in LaunchArgs reaches every migrated bench without editing the bench. New dev scripts get a parser the ratchet allows, so direct_cmdline_reads can shrink instead of being argued up at every merge (baseline.json records 5 accepted rises on 2026-11-06/07).

## Evaluation
Claim: one declared parser removes the duplicated parse loops and the silent acceptance on the paths lanes run most.
Before: 87 dev files / 90 raw reads with hand loops; 20 accept unknown args silently; 19 local KNOWN lists; ArenaArgs accepts any arg (41 flags via 13 files); direct_cmdline_reads 157; 3 lane FRICTION lines on 2026-11-07 about it (perf l.117, hud l.48, handheld l.656).
After: 11 entry points (ArenaArgs + 10 scripts) on ArgSpec, all rejecting unknown args with exit 2 and a hint; none of them keeps a local list repeating LaunchArgs flags; direct_cmdline_reads <= 147 and falling as scripts migrate.
Method: probe - counted reads, quit(2) sites, KNOWN lists and ArenaArgs readers with grep; diffed city_bench KNOWN_FLAGS against LaunchArgs.KNOWN_FLAGS with node -e; read direct_cmdline_reads from baseline.json.
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: grep get_cmdline_user_args project/dev: 90 reads in 87 files; of them 66 contain quit(2), 20 contain neither quit(2) nor "unknown"; 19 files declare KNOWN_FLAGS/KNOWN/KEYS; ArenaArgs read in 13 dev files, 41 distinct flags via args.has/text/number; city_bench KNOWN_FLAGS has 13 entries, 4 also in LaunchArgs.KNOWN_FLAGS (53); baseline.json direct_cmdline_reads total 157, 87 of them in project/dev; quit() spellings in dev: quit(2) x77, quit(0) x30, quit(exit_code) x28, quit(0 if ok else 1) x12, quit(1) x11, plus 5 others.

body:
## Summary
One Node front door for every dev scene or -s script: node tools/dev/run.mjs <entry> [flags]. Before launch it resolves the entry (scene or -s script) and puts the scene path and the -- where they belong. It checks each flag against the entry's declared spec, read statically from the .gd (card A's ArgSpec const, falling back to a KNOWN list const), and refuses a wrong one in under a second. It derives --fixed-fps/--quit-after from a declared RUN_TICKS. After exit it prints one verdict line built from the exit code, SCRIPT ERROR lines, unknown-arg warnings and whether the result file is fresh. tools/lib/dev_verdict.mjs is the same judgement as a library, and tools/selftest/run.mjs adopts it.

## Description
The users are the lanes that film A/B befores and afters many times an hour. Their most repeated loss on 2026-11-06/07 is a film of the wrong scene: arena flags passed without res://dev/arena/arena.tscn, or after a stray --, which boot.gd:10 only warns about. That is 8 FRICTION lines (chars 21/234/304, hud 50/165/1294, rivet 388/707), each a wasted run of minutes. The second is guessing --quit-after for reels whose length the script already knows (rivet 175, 602). The third is that no runner states the verdict: lanes grep their logs and write "0 SCRIPT ERROR, 0 unknown arg" into REPORTs by hand, and the selftest runner itself drops two exit statuses. This is not a flag registry: the tool reads each entry's own declaration at call time, and there is no list file, owner or expiry.

## Flow
- entries.mjs: resolve(name|path) -> {kind: scene|script, path, flags, runTicks}. A bare name searches project/dev/**/<name>.{tscn,gd}. Flags are parsed from the entry's const spec and its *_args.gd helper (e.g. boot/arena_args.gd).
- run.mjs: pre-flight first (an unknown flag exits 2 with a did-you-mean and nothing is spawned). It builds args through runGodot, so the ledger, the import preflight and the tree-kill still apply. Headless by default, --windowed opt-in; the log goes to build/dev/<entry>-<time>.log.
- dev_verdict.mjs: verdict({status, out, timedOut}, {resultFile, startedAt}) -> {ok, line, scriptErrors[], unknownArgs[]}. Exit codes read as 0 ok / 1 fail / 2 usage / -1 never ran, plus timeout.
- tools/selftest/run.mjs: runLookGolden, runAccentAudit, runWorldLock and runSelftest pass their result through verdict, so an exit 1 or a SCRIPT ERROR can no longer pass behind an ok JSON.
- reel_director.gd declares RUN_TICKS from its existing total, so the reel's --quit-after is derived.

## Expected impact
The wrong-scene film becomes a refused command before Godot starts. The reel length stops being a guess. Every dev run ends in one line a lane can paste into its REPORT, and selftest evidence stops passing on a failed exit.

## Evaluation
Claim: a pre-flight plus a single verdict line removes the lanes' most repeated dev-run loss and their hand-assembled verdicts.
Before: 8 wrong-scene/stray-separator FRICTION lines in 3 lanes over 2026-11-06/07 (chars x3, hud x3, rivet x2); 2 --quit-after-too-short lines (rivet 175, 602); hand-written "0 SCRIPT ERROR / 0 unknown arg" verdicts in the calls and held REPORTs; 2 of 4 selftest stages ignore the exit status; 2 of 10 runGodot callers scan for SCRIPT_ERROR.
After: each of those 8 commands exits 2 in under 1 s and names the scene or the flag; the reel's --quit-after is derived; one verdict line per run; all 4 selftest stages and every run.mjs launch judged by verdict.
Method: probe - grepped FRICTION lines in docs/day/2026-11-0{6,7}/*/JOURNAL.md, the REPORT verdict lines, SCRIPT_ERROR importers across tools/**/*.mjs and the awaits in tools/selftest/run.mjs.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: FRICTION lines: chars/JOURNAL.md:21,234,304; hud/JOURNAL.md:50,165,1294; rivet/JOURNAL.md:388,707 (wrong scene / stray --); rivet/JOURNAL.md:175,602 (--quit-after too short). REPORTs: calls/REPORT.md:42,55,59,67,69,71 and held/REPORT.md:7,82 hand-write "0 SCRIPT ERROR"/"no unknown-arg warning". grep SCRIPT_ERROR tools: only run_unit.mjs:19 and perf/ab.mjs:18 import it, of 10 runGodot callers. tools/selftest/run.mjs:62 and :91 are bare awaits (no status read).

checked: Read tools/lib/godot.mjs (SCRIPT_ERROR l.19, runGodot, removeStale), tools/selftest/run.mjs, the head of tools/bench/run.mjs, the runGodot caller list and the SCRIPT_ERROR importers. Hypothesis: runners trust a dev script's JSON without its exit code or log. Confirmed: selftest run.mjs:62 and :91 drop the exit status, and only run_unit and perf/ab scan for SCRIPT ERROR. Today's fixes (strict CLI args, ledger guard, double import) do not touch this. Card B targets the seam: tools/lib/dev_verdict.mjs, adopted by selftest. A shared CLI parser for the Node runners is open backlog, so no card went there.
